job.title: The job

colleague.prose: Knows essentially the entire written world. Extremely confident. Eager to please.

colleague-not-tool.header: Why a colleague and not a tool
colleague-not-tool.description: Vendors and practitioners independently frame the model as a brilliant newcomer who lacks context on your norms, which is why the test works for non-coders too.[1]

same-lens.description: Matt Pocock describes an agent as a colleague who starts afresh every session, and Mollick’s current form is an “infinitely patient new coworker who forgets everything”.[1][2]

intern-wrong-rank.description: Mollick dropped the intern wording in 2024 because it makes people use AI in constrained ways; “colleague” is the supported form.[1]

the-job.title: The job
the-job.script: It is Monday morning. You must plan the company Sommerfest. Or the Christmas party, pick your season. About a hundred people. A fully structured plan has to be on your team lead's desk, or the CEO's, by end of day.

who-walks-in.title: Who walks in
who-walks-in.script: And help has arrived. A new colleague, on their very first day. They know essentially the entire written world. Every book on event planning, every review of every venue. They are extremely confident. And eager to please. They will say yes to anything.

take-a-second.title: Take a second
take-a-second.script: Take a second. Really. The clock is running, and they are standing at your desk. What do you say?
